title: States of matter & changes
examples: What is the difference between melting and boiling?
Can a substance change directly from a solid to a gas?
How do the particles move in a gas compared to a liquid?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the three common states of matter.

draw.text: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, Gas

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: solid, liquid and gas. Look at the solid, the liquid and the gas. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
A solid has particles packed closely in fixed positions.
A liquid has particles close but can slide past each other.
A gas has particles far apart and moving randomly fast.
Melting is the change from a solid to a liquid state.
Boiling is the change from a liquid to a gas state.

faq.q: What is the difference between melting and boiling?
faq.a: Melting is when a solid turns into a liquid. Boiling is when a liquid turns into a gas.
asks: How do I know if it is melting or boiling?
What is the change from solid to liquid called?
Is melting the same as boiling?

faq.q: Does temperature always determine the state?
faq.a: Temperature is important, but pressure can also change the state of matter. For example, some substances can be liquid or gas at the same temperature.
asks: Can pressure change the state of matter?
Do I need pressure to change states?

faq.a: Sublimation is when a solid changes directly into a gas without becoming a liquid first. Think about dry ice.
asks: What is the solid to gas change?
Does it ever skip the liquid stage?
What is the name for solid to gas change?

facts: Solids have particles that vibrate in fixed positions.
Liquids can flow because their particles can slide past each other.
Gases have particles that move rapidly and spread out to fill any container.
Sublimation is the process of solid changing directly to gas.

quiz.say: Which state has particles packed closely but can slide past each other?
quiz.why: Liquids have particles that are close together but not fixed, allowing them to flow.

wrong.1: Solids have particles that are fixed in place, so they cannot flow easily.
wrong.2: Gases have particles that are too far apart to be considered 'close' enough to slide past each other.
wrong.3: Plasma is a fourth state, but the question only asks about the three main states.

quiz.say: When ice turns into water, what process is occurring?
quiz.why: Melting is the specific name for the change from the solid state to the liquid state.

wrong.0: Condensation is the change from gas back to liquid, which is the reverse process.
wrong.1: Sublimation is the change directly from solid to gas, skipping the liquid phase.
wrong.3: Boiling is the change from liquid to gas, which is a different process.

quiz.say: Dry ice turning into gas shows which change?
quiz.why: Sublimation is the process where a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid stage.

wrong.0: Boiling must start with a liquid that is already present.
wrong.1: Evaporation is a surface process, but sublimation describes the direct solid-to-gas change.
wrong.3: Melting requires the solid to first turn into a liquid before changing state.
